instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: Individuals within the same social class often share similar life chances and opportunities.
Social inequality describes the concept of equal life chances for all groups in society no matter their family background, social class and economic status.

wrong.text: Social inequality describes the unequal opportunities of groups within society.

atoms.a: Social mobility refers to the movement of individuals or groups upwards or downwards within the social hierarchy.
Social stratification describes the concept of ranking individuals based on their personal achievements and talent.

wrong.text: Social stratification describes the hierarchical ranking of people into groups based on socioeconomic factors like income, wealth and occupation.

atoms.a: Occupational prestige describes how jobs are ranked according to their financial value.

wrong.text: Occupational prestige describes how jobs are ranked socially, making it subjective and variable between different societies and cultures.

atoms.a: Economic status includes both an individual's income and wealth.
Individuals who are part of the „working class“ are typically working in office environments.

wrong.text: The working class typically performs manual or physical labor.

atoms.a: The lower class is a social class characterized by lower income and the lack of long-term job security with low prestige.
The broad middle class is often characterised by higher education such as university degrees or specialised certifications.
The upper class is considered the highest social class of the hierarchy, consisting only of a small percentage of the population.
Etiquette describes social rules and manners within societies and social groups and is exactly the same in every country and culture around the world.

wrong.text: Etiquette describes social rules and manners within societies and social groups and is different in every country and culture.

atoms.a: Meritocracy describes a system where being successful is linked to hard work, effort and talent.
A stigma refers to attaching a negative label to an individual based on social stereotypes. Stigmatised people experience exclusion.
Income describes the money an individual gets paid on a regular basis, usually as wages from a job.
